# Wire the model classes through the code-review gate (they are declared and ignored)

**Filed as a bug, RECLASSIFIED AS A STORY on operator direction: this is the epic's wiring work — carrying the three-class configuration through the review process — not a defect repair. The observable symptom below is what proves the wiring is absent.**

## Problem

`code-review.yaml` declares a model CLASS on all five of its LLM-calling steps, and **every one of
those declarations is silently ignored at runtime.** The gate runs every pass on the single resolved
`cfg.model`, which is exactly the one-knob behaviour epic 061c exists to remove.

MEASURED, not inferred. A real `rebar review-code` run with `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` (one JSON record per
LLM call, written at the runner chokepoint `llm/runner.py:545`) under an INVERTED class config
(`frontier = bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8`, `standard = anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6`):

    1 code-review-base                             anthropic:claude-opus-4-8   <- declares frontier
    2 code-review-docs                             anthropic:claude-opus-4-8
    3 code-review-tests                            anthropic:claude-opus-4-8
    4 code-review-deletion-impact                  anthropic:claude-opus-4-8
    5 code-review-project-review-phase-boundaries  anthropic:claude-opus-4-8
    6 code-review-api-compat                       anthropic:claude-opus-4-8
    7 code-review-verify                            anthropic:claude-opus-4-8   <- declares standard
    8 code-review-coach                             anthropic:claude-opus-4-8   <- declares standard
    9 code-novelty                                  anthropic:claude-opus-4-8

Nine calls, all on the bare default. `verify` has declared `model: standard` since story 172e
closed, so **this is a pre-existing defect, not a regression** introduced by 3768.

## Three competing explanations; two eliminated by experiment

This is recorded because each cheaper probe produced the SAME observation, and only the discriminating
one settles it.

- **H3 — the class table falls back to built-in defaults** (the run is scoped to a snapshot read root
  via `gate_source.gate_read_root(handle)`, so a config-file class table might not be visible).
  **ELIMINATED:** `_DEFAULT_MODEL_BY_CLASS['standard'] == 'claude-sonnet-4-6'`, so under H3 `verify`
  would have run on SONNET. It ran on OPUS.
- **H2 — the config pointer was never loaded.** **ELIMINATED:** with the same env var,
  `load_class_slots()` -> `resolve_class('frontier')` returns `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8`,
  both with and without `repo_root=` (the form the gate uses).
- **H1 — the step's `model:` never reaches the resolver. CONFIRMED.** It is the only hypothesis that
  predicts opus for a step declaring `standard`. Corroborated directly:
  `resolve_model(cfg, step='frontier')` -> `bedrock:...` while `resolve_model(cfg, step=None)` ->
  `claude-opus-4-8`, which is precisely what was logged.

Also ruled out: the running package loads the worktree's own gate file with all five declarations
intact, and `code_review/shim.py:119 review_code` really does execute the gate via
`gate_dispatch.produce_code_review_verdict`.

## The lead: an asymmetry with the gate that DOES work

The plan-review gate honours classes — a live two-provider run showed a 41/1 opus/sonnet split across
providers. The dispatch paths differ in a way that is a concrete starting point rather than a guess:

- plan-review (`gate_dispatch.py` ~:146-163) wraps `run_workflow` in **`gate_config(cfg)`**, whose own
  comment says it "publishes `cfg` so every op (and the non-step ProductionBatchRunner) reads the SAME
  resolved config via `resolve_gate_config` instead of re-deriving from env".
- code-review (`gate_dispatch.py` ~:414-424) wraps only
  `gate_source.gate_read_root(handle), review_kernel.collect_contract_violations()` — **no
  `gate_config(cfg)`**.

Whether that omission is the cause or merely adjacent must be established before fixing; do not assume
it. `workflow/runs.py:154` does pass `step=ctx.step.get("model")` into `resolve_model`, and
`code_review/batch_runner.py:60-61,83-84` does resolve `req.model_ladder[0]` and set `step["model"]`,
so both halves look correct in isolation — the defect is in what actually executes for this gate.

## Approach

### STEP 0 (FIRST, and it is a deliverable in its own right): make the usage log able to attribute a call to a STEP.

`llm/usage_log.py` records `op=` — the PROMPT NAME — and nothing else that identifies the caller. That is why the nine-call log CANNOT locate this: `code-review-base` is the prompt used BOTH by the `base`
step AND as the `batch:` finder for `round_a`/`round_b`, so no observed record can be attributed to a
step. Diagnosing on top of that would mean guessing which path produced which call, and guessing from
an instrument that cannot see the distinction is how three earlier probes in this epic produced
confident wrong answers.

So the first change is OBSERVABILITY, not a fix: record the STEP ID (and the resolved model's declared
CLASS, when the value came from a class token) alongside `op` on every usage record. Properties this
must have: it is additive (existing consumers keep working — `summarize()` folds the file for
`$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`), it stays a no-op when `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` is unset, and it makes the CURRENT
defect visible as data rather than inference. Re-running the live probe after Step 0 is what turns
"nine calls on cfg.model" into "step X received model Y", which names the broken seam directly.

This also outlives the ticket: every future per-pass or per-provider question in this epic (0d76's
parity arms, eb6e's cutover, 8625's docs) needs exactly this attribution, and 0d76's own research
already assumes "the REBAR_USAGE_LOG rig records per-call model" — it records the model but not the
step, which is the half that matters for a per-PASS claim.

### Then the wiring

Diagnose first, then fix the narrowest seam. Trace one `base` call from `produce_code_review_verdict`
to the runner and identify where the declared class is dropped. Fix that seam so a declared class
reaches `resolve_model`/`resolve_model_string` for BOTH single-shot prompt steps and batch steps.

This ticket does NOT change any declaration in `code-review.yaml` — 3768 already made those correct,
and 172e's `verify` declaration is correct too. Only the plumbing changes.

## Scope

**STEP 0 — observability. These were previously listed in `file_impact` but NOT enumerated here; a
review round blocked four times on that single inconsistency, so they are spelled out.**

- `src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py` — **the primary Step 0 target.** Add the step id (and the declared
  CLASS when the model came from a class token) to what `record()` writes, and keep `summarize()`
  working on the new shape. `record()` must stay a no-op when `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` is unset.
- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — **the only `usage_log.record()` call site, VERIFIED: `:547`**, called as
  `record(usage, op=_call_label, model=ran_model, provider=infer_provider(ran_model))`. `op` is derived
  from `_call_label`, which is why the log currently carries the PROMPT name and not the step.
  THE THREADING PROBLEM, stated because it is the real design decision in Step 0: `RunRequest`
  (`runner.py:~69`) has fields `system_prompt`, `instructions`, `config`, `reviewers`, `target`,
  `langfuse_prompt` — and **no step id**. So the step must reach `:547` by one of:
    (a) a new `RunRequest` field — explicit and typed, but touches every construction site;
    (b) the existing `target: dict` — no signature change, but overloads a field meaning something else;
    (c) a ContextVar set by the step executor and read at the record call — no signature churn, and it
        mirrors the existing precedent of `_active_gate_config` in `llm/config.py`.
  Pick ONE and record why; do not leave it to the implementer.
- `src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py` — **NOT expected to change.** Named only to close the question: it
  emits the per-call caching warning that misled an earlier probe (it fires only when caching was
  requested and had no effect, so it captured 3 of 9 calls), but it does NOT call `usage_log.record`.
  If Step 0 turns out to need a change here, that is new information worth a comment.
  **DELIBERATELY ABSENT FROM `file_impact`** — that field records files this ticket IMPACTS, and this
  one is named here only to close the question of whether it is involved. The asymmetry is intentional,
  not an oversight; every other file named in this Scope IS in `file_impact` (checked mechanically).

**THE WIRING FIX — the seam is NOT yet identified, and Step 0 exists to identify it.** Expect to change
ONE of these; do not change all three speculatively:
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py` — the code-review dispatch path (~:414-424), which omits the
  `gate_config(cfg)` scope the working plan-review path uses (~:146-163).
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/runs.py` — `RunnerAgentStep.run` (~:144-156) for single-shot prompt steps; it
  already reads `ctx.step.get("model")`, so if the drop is here it is upstream of this read.
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/batch_runner.py` — `CodeReviewBatchRunner` (~:60-61, :83-84) for batch
  steps; it already resolves `model_ladder[0]` and sets `step["model"]`.

**READ ONLY:**
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/code-review.yaml` — the five declarations are already correct (3768 and
  172e) and MUST NOT change. If a fix appears to require editing them, the diagnosis is wrong.

- `tests/` — the usage-log attribution test and the end-to-end recording-runner test.


## Testing

**The missing test is the point of this ticket, not an afterthought.** 3768 shipped 9 tests and a 6/6
mutation score and STILL missed this, because every assertion checked either YAML content or
`resolve_model_string(<token>)` in isolation. Nothing observed the ENGINE PASSING the token to the
resolver, so no mutation could distinguish "declaration honoured" from "declaration ignored".

- END-TO-END, offline: execute the code-review gate with a RECORDING runner (a fake that captures the
  model it is handed per step) and assert each of the five steps receives its declared class. This is
  deterministic and free; it is strictly stronger than a live probe and it is the guard that would
  have caught this.
- the same test must FAIL on today's code — confirm RED before fixing.
- a mutation that removes the fix must break it (assert the anchor exists AND that the text changed;
  a mutation that silently no-ops looks identical to a test that cannot detect).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] every `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` record carries the STEP ID of the step that made the call, in addition to
      the existing `op` (prompt name). Asserted by a test that runs a gate with the log enabled and
      checks the recorded step ids — NOT by reading `usage_log.py`. Without this the log cannot
      distinguish the `base` step from the `round_a`/`round_b` batch finder, because both use the prompt
      `code-review-base`, and no per-PASS claim about this gate is checkable.
- [ ] a record whose model came from a CLASS token also carries that class, so a reader can tell
      "resolved to opus because frontier" from "resolved to opus because cfg.model" — the exact
      ambiguity that made three earlier probes in this epic unfalsifiable.
- [ ] the addition is ADDITIVE and inert when unconfigured: `summarize()` still folds a log written by
      the new writer, and `record()` remains a no-op when `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` is unset (asserted).
- [ ] [operator-attested] the live probe is RE-RUN after Step 0 and the resulting PER-STEP attribution
      is recorded in a comment — this is the DIAGNOSTIC run that names the broken seam, and it
      replaces inference with data. Tagged because it is an inherently external artifact (a live LLM
      run whose output is pasted into a comment) and the verifier cannot confirm it from code —
      exactly the untagged-external-evidence trap this epic has hit repeatedly.
      DISTINCT from the final live-run criterion below: this one runs on the BROKEN code to locate
      the seam; that one runs after the fix to show the declarations are honoured. Both are needed
      and neither substitutes for the other.

- [ ] an offline end-to-end test executes the code-review gate with a recording runner and asserts
      that EACH of the five LLM steps (`base`, `round_a`, `round_b`, `verify`, `coach`) receives its
      DECLARED class, not `cfg.model` — and it is observed RED on the pre-fix code
- [ ] the same test covers BOTH shapes: a single-shot prompt step (`base`, step-level `model:`) and a
      batch step (`round_a`, `batch.model_ladder`), because they travel different code paths
- [ ] a test asserts that under a class table whose values differ from `cfg.model`, NO step resolves
      to `cfg.model` — the assertion that discriminates "honoured" from "ignored"
- [ ] `verify`'s pre-existing `model: standard` (172e) is shown to be honoured by the same test, so
      this closes 172e's latent evidence gap rather than only 3768's
- [ ] no declaration in `code-review.yaml` is changed by this ticket
- [ ] [operator-attested] a real `rebar review-code` run with `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` under a class table
      whose classes differ from `cfg.model` shows the per-pass model ids matching the declarations,
      cited from the JSONL in a comment — the run that currently DISPROVES the behaviour
